description: Light/parchment reading mode + dark/ink default, with an accessible NavBar theme toggle. Uses Tailwind darkMode:'class'. This is the trickiest, most cross-cutting feature and is done FIRST so later features author their new UI theme-aware. Independent of FEAT-002/003/004 in logic, but ordered first because it touches ArgumentCard (which FEAT-003 also edits) and establishes the theming conventions the whole UI pass relies on.
steps: In tailwind.config.js add `darkMode: 'class'` at the top of the exported config object (sibling of `content` and `theme`). No palette changes — ink/parchment/gold scales already exist.

In index.html: set <html lang="en" class="dark"> and add a tiny no-flash inline <script> in <head> BEFORE the module script. The script reads localStorage.getItem('theme'); if 'light' remove the 'dark' class, if 'dark' add it, else fall back to window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches to decide. It must run synchronously so there is no flash of the wrong theme before React mounts.

Make src/index.css theme-aware: the @layer base body rule currently `@apply bg-ink-900 text-parchment-100`. Change to a light base with a dark override, e.g. `@apply bg-parchment-100 text-ink-900` and add a `.dark body { @apply bg-ink-900 text-parchment-100; }` rule (or use Tailwind's `dark:` on the body via a class). Update `:focus-visible` ring-offset-color so the ring reads in both themes (e.g. offset parchment in light, ink-900 in dark). ::selection can stay gold/ink. Keep overflow-x guard and h1-h6 color theme-aware (dark text in light mode).

Audit and convert every component with hardcoded ink/parchment/gold colors to light-base + `dark:` overrides, keeping the CURRENT value as the dark override and choosing a readable light-mode base. Convert: src/components/Layout.tsx (footer bg/borders, skip-link bg/text), src/components/NavBar.tsx (header bg/backdrop, link active/hover states, desktop search box, kbd, mobile panel bg + items, icon colors), src/components/SearchModal.tsx (backdrop bg, panel bg/border/shadow, divider, result rows active/hover, citation chips, kbd footer — DO NOT change any search behavior/logic).

Convert content components: src/components/ArgumentCard.tsx (card bg/border/shadow, title, shortClaim, explanation text), src/components/Callout.tsx (all four variant container+title classes AND the shared body text class), src/components/SectionHeader.tsx (bottom border, title, count), src/components/StrengthBadge.tsx (give each of the three CONFIG classNames a light-mode-readable base with dark override — gold 'scriptural' solid stays legible both ways; 'strong' amber outline; 'supplementary' muted), src/components/ReferenceBlock.tsx (figure bg/left-border, cite, translation chip, blockquote text), src/components/OriginalLanguageBlock.tsx (bg/border, language label, text, translit, note).

Convert pages: src/pages/Home.tsx (hero eyebrow/title/subtitle/divider/lead, live topic cards border/bg/hover/text, coming-soon cards), src/pages/TopicPage.tsx (back link, heading, subtitle, intro-callout wrapper, caveats <details> border/bg/summary/items, not-found and coming-soon states), src/pages/NotFound.tsx (eyebrow/title/body/link).

Add the theme toggle to src/components/NavBar.tsx: a button rendered in both the desktop control cluster and the mobile cluster (or a single button visible in both) that toggles the 'dark' class on document.documentElement and persists localStorage.setItem('theme', next). Use a sun icon in dark mode / moon icon in light mode (inline SVG, matching existing icon style). Give it aria-pressed reflecting dark state, an aria-label like 'Switch to light theme'/'Switch to dark theme', min 44x44 tap target, gold hover styling consistent with the other NavBar buttons. Initialize the button's state from document.documentElement.classList.contains('dark') on mount (via useState initializer or useEffect) so it matches the no-flash script with no hydration flash. Optionally extract a small src/hooks/useTheme.ts hook used by NavBar.

Update README.md: add a short 'Reading mode (light / dark)' section documenting the parchment light theme vs ink dark default, the NavBar toggle, localStorage persistence, and prefers-color-scheme on first visit.
acceptance_criteria: index.html head contains a synchronous inline script that sets/removes the 'dark' class from localStorage['theme'] with prefers-color-scheme fallback, and <html> defaults to class="dark".
All audited components and pages render with correct, WCAG AA-contrast colors in BOTH the dark (ink) and light (parchment) themes — no element is invisible or low-contrast in either theme.
NavBar has an accessible theme toggle (aria-pressed + aria-label, >=44px) that flips the theme and persists it; no flash of the wrong theme on reload.
npm run build and npm run typecheck both exit 0 with no TypeScript errors.
Brand name 'Ave Christus Rex' is unchanged; no reintroduction of 'Ave Jesus Rex'. Search behavior unchanged.
verification: Run `npm run build` from repo root — must exit 0 (tsc + vite build clean).
Read dist/index.html and confirm the inline no-flash script and class="dark" are present.
Grep the compiled CSS (dist/assets/*.css) to confirm both base and `.dark` variant rules were emitted (e.g. search for `.dark` occurrences).
Do NOT start a dev server or run preview (port 5317 is in use). Reason about both themes from the compiled CSS/markup.
findings:
THEMING CONVENTIONS (follow these for all later features so new UI is theme-aware):
- Tailwind darkMode:'class' is enabled. The authoritative state is the `dark` class on <html>, set synchronously by the no-flash <script> in index.html (reads localStorage['theme'] 'light'/'dark', else prefers-color-scheme, default dark) BEFORE the module script.
- PATTERN: author LIGHT as the base utility and put the OLD dark value behind a `dark:` variant. Example: `bg-parchment-50 ... dark:bg-ink-800/40`, `text-ink-900 dark:text-parchment-50`, `border-ink-200/70 dark:border-ink-600/50`. NEVER write a bare dark-only `text-parchment-*`/`bg-ink-*` without a light base.
- STANDARD COLOR MAP used (dark override -> light base):
  * body/base text: text-parchment-100 -> text-ink-900 (handled globally in index.css via `.dark body` + `.dark h1..h6`; headings also handled globally).
  * card/surface bg: bg-ink-800/40 -> bg-parchment-50 ; secondary surface bg-ink-900/60 -> bg-parchment-200/60.
  * card border: border-ink-600/50 -> border-ink-200/70.
  * primary body copy: text-parchment-200 -> text-ink-700 ; strong copy text-parchment-100 -> text-ink-800.
  * muted copy: text-parchment-300/400 -> text-ink-500/600 ; faint/disabled text-parchment-500 -> text-ink-400.
  * gold accents/links: text-gold-200/300/400 -> text-gold-600/700 (gold-700 for text on light; gold-500 solid dividers/rings stay as-is both themes).
  * chips/kbd bg: bg-ink-700/70 -> bg-ink-200/70 (text text-parchment-300/400 -> text-ink-500/600).
  * active nav/row: bg-gold-900/30 -> bg-gold-900/15.
- index.css now has: light `body` base + `.dark body` override; `:focus-visible` uses ring-gold-500 + ring-offset-parchment-100, with `.dark :focus-visible` -> ring-gold-300 + ring-offset-ink-900. ::selection unchanged (gold/ink, fine in both). h1-h6 default text-ink-900 with `.dark` -> text-parchment-50.
- StrengthBadge: 'scriptural' stays solid gold-400 on ink-900 (legible both themes); 'strong' and 'supplementary' got light bases with dark: overrides.
- NavBar is a sticky header: `sticky top-0 z-40`, padding py-3 (approx 60-64px tall). Content uses scroll-mt-24 (6rem) for hash anchors, already clearing the sticky header. The theme toggle lives in NavBar at all breakpoints via a shared `useTheme()` hook at src/hooks/useTheme.ts (returns {theme,isDark,toggleTheme}; initializes from document.documentElement.classList to match the no-flash script, no hydration flash). Toggle button is 44x44 (h-11 w-11), aria-pressed + aria-label.
- NO git repo exists in this worktree (only a .gitignore, `git rev-parse` fails), so NO commit was made per instructions ('unless the workspace is not a repository'). Later features likewise cannot commit until a repo is initialized.
- VERIFIED: `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` both exit 0; dist/index.html contains the no-flash script + class="dark"; dist/assets CSS contains 114 `.dark` rule occurrences incl. `.dark body`.
